plan: This mechanism effectively replicates a second-price sealed-bid auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such auctions, truthful bidding (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever the value exceeds the price I'd pay, and never overpays. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $25.

This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid, and my exit point is determined by my own bid. Since payment doesn't depend on my own bid (only on the second-highest), truthful bidding is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value of $17 ensures I win whenever profitable (value exceeds price) and avoid losses otherwise. No history to adjust from since this is the only round.

This is structurally equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point in the clock stage is determined by my sealed bid. Since payment depends on others' bids, not my own, bidding my true value ($39) is the dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.
